AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #20
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Heating until a solid melts

3. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Nitrogen gas only
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Only water vapour

4. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Decomposers only
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Producers

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Growing Trees? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Growing Trees.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Growing Trees.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Growing Trees.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Trees.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Establishment Planting Site? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Establishment Planting Site.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production ? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Conserving Food Nutrients? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Food Nutrients.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Conserving Food Nutrients.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Conserving Food Nutrients.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Conserving Food Nutrients.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Making Homemade Soap and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Controlling Soil Pollution and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Constructing Water Retention Structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Conserving Food Nutrients and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

3. B — Glucose and oxygen

4. D — Producers

5. D — 100 °C

6. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

7. B — Ice melting to water

8. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food 9 3.0 Hygiene Practises 3.1 Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundr.

9. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Growing Trees.

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Establishment Planting Site.

11. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hygiene in Rearing Animals 9 3.2 Laundry: Loose-coloured Items 8 4.0 Production .

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Conserving Food Nutrients.
